chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, who said:

I wrote to him (peace be upon him): May I be made your sacrifice from every evil! A woman breastfed a baby female goat until she was weaned, and she grew up, and the stallion mounted her, then she gave birth. Is it permissible to eat its flesh and its milk? So he wrote (peace be upon him): It is an abhorrent deed, and there is no problem with it.

key_terms.الْفَحْلُ: The stud male/stallion — a male animal used for breeding
key_terms.عَنَاقاً: Baby female goat (anaq) — the young of a goat before it can graze independently
key_terms.فُطِمَتْ: Was weaned — when nursing ceases and the young is separated from the source of milk
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: There is no problem with it — standard legal formula affirming permissibility
key_terms.مَكْرُوهٌ: Makruh — jurisprudential category of 'disapproved' acts: not forbidden (haram) but religiously discouraged

ai.seo_question: What did the Imam say about eating the meat and milk of a goat that was breastfed by a woman?
ai.summary: Ahmad ibn Muhammad writes to the Imam (peace be upon him) asking about a woman who breastfed a baby female goat until it was weaned, grew up, was mated with a male, and gave birth. The Imam replies that this act is makruh (reprehensible/disapproved) but that consuming the offspring's meat and milk is nonetheless permissible. This concise ruling illustrates the Shia jurisprudential principle that makruh acts do not render their outcomes unlawful — disapproval does not equate to prohibition (haram).

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad who said,

‘I wrote to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup> from every evil! A woman breast-fed a baby female goat until she weaned it, and she grew big, and the stallion struck her, then she gave birth. Is it allowable to eat its flesh, and its milk?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> wrote: ‘An abhorrent deed, and there is no problem with it’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from who has said the following: “

I once wrote to him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause against all evil, a woman has breastfed a young she-goat and weaned it. It grew up and gave birth. Is it permissible to use its milk and flesh for food?’ He (the Imam) wrote back saying, ‘It is an undesirable act but it is not unlawful.’ ”
